text:
alex: night huddle — quick async handoff. TL;DR: 1) routing surge impacting ap-sg1 -> rex-route p99 ~450ms (normal ~120ms). 2) eu-west dedicated autoscaler is oscillating after canary, observed several scale-downs then immediate scale-ups. I patched a temporary routing weight to favor replicas in ap-sg2.

alex: what I did: pulled logs from router and edge-proxy, bumped routing weight, disabled the small-capacity canary in eu-west (ref: canary-2026-03-16), posted a muted alert to pagerduty and annotated the incident. Ran quick heap checks on the router pods.

alex: commands I ran (if needed):
```
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=rex-router -o wide
kubectl -n redwood logs rex-router-78c9f -c router | grep "latency" -A3
rdwctl routing adjust --from ap-sg1 --to ap-sg2 --weight 0.35
```

alex: blockers: still unclear if the ap-sg1 spike is due to a noisy customer or network flaps — noticed a jump in outbound BGP resets ~03:12 UTC. Need net team to confirm. Also autoscaler policy tune for eu-west requires product signoff before we make it permanent.

priya: thanks alex. I can reach out to netops, pinging @samuel and @maria for visibility. Any cluster/node IDs you want me to highlight? :eyes:

alex: priya — ta. the noisy nodes are ap-sg1-node-7 and -9, both showing elevated retransmits. traced a few requests tied to a single tenant (tenant-id: t-93f4). I left a note in the incident doc.

samuel: on it, paged netops. quick check: does traffic still route correctly to ap-sg2? any error spike?

alex: samuel — routing to ap-sg2 is healthy, no 5xx surge. throughput is ~90% normal; p50/p95 unchanged. Most impact is increased tail.

maria: eu-west autoscaler — I dug into the HPA logs, looks like an aggressive cpu threshold (40%) + short stabilization window (30s). I suggest a conservative change to 60% / 2m stabilization. I can prepare a PR for the scaler config.

ben: @maria please do the PR but hold from deploying until after morning sync with product. We'll need to capture perf regression tests.

alex: noted. For now I set a temporary manual min-replicas to 6 in eu-west to stop thrash. If we need to roll it back later I'll leave instructions in the runbook.

ops-bot: [ALERT] routing.p99.ap-sg1 exceeded threshold at 2026-03-16T03:11:52Z — value: 452ms — triggered by probe cluster-monitor. Incident ID: INC-20260316-92.

priya: added netops ticket NET-3781 and linked node metrics. I'll escalate if we see more resets.

samuel: netops responded — they see a partial transit flap between vendor-edge-a and our ap-sg1 VPC. They are opening a bridge and will track. ETA unknown.

alex: next steps (short):
- priya: confirm NET-3781 bridge notes and update here (status + ETA).
- maria: PR for autoscaler tune (draft, don't deploy).
- ben: coordinate product check in tomorrow AM before autoscaler change.
- samuel: follow netops bridge and post any immediate mitigation they suggest.

alex: final notes: if ap-sg1 recovers, I'll gradually revert routing weight over 30m and monitor. If netops confirms sustained instability, we'll initiate shift to ap-sg2 as primary until patch. Leaving the bridge open and my pager reachable. :thumbsup:

priya: acked, will update NET-3781 with logs and an initial timeline.

maria: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/452 — description includes perf checks.

ben: added this to tomorrow AM agenda. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks team — handing off to morning crew. I'm available if anything spikes.
